title: MetadataProvider's sessionStorage app cache is keyed by type only — after an org switch the landing resolves from the PREVIOUS org's app list (and a cached `[]` short-circuits initialLoading)
body:
Measured during #4473 (PR #4483's landing-chain trace). Two defects in one mechanism, filed together because the fix is one keying decision.

## What

`MetadataProvider` seeds from sessionStorage (`objectui:metadata:app`) **keyed by metadata TYPE only, not by organization**, and clears `loading` before the org-scoped fetch returns. Consequences, measured on the #4473 repro chain:

1. **Cross-org staleness drives real decisions**: after a workspace switch (full-page reload to the console root), `RootLandingRedirect` resolves its landing rules against the PREVIOUS org's cached app list — that is precisely what aimed a fresh-workspace member at `/apps/setup` in #4473. The strand it caused is fixed (PR #4483 bounces), but the resolver is still consuming another org's data during the seed window; any other consumer of `useMetadata().apps` in that window inherits the same wrong answer.
2. **Truthy-empty short-circuit**: `loadFromSession` returning `[]` is truthy, so an empty CACHED list also suppresses `initialLoading` — "no apps (cached, possibly stale)" is indistinguishable from "no apps (fresh)".

## Fix shape (for whoever takes it)

Key the cache by org (include the active org identifier in the storage key, or invalidate on org change), and treat a cached empty list as a miss for the `initialLoading` decision. Both are the same one-line class once the keying is decided.

## Why filed rather than fixed in #4473

Out of that card's ruled surface (its fix is the app-surface bounce; this is the provider). No user-visible strand remains after PR #4483, so this is currently a wrong-mechanism defect with reduced blast radius — but stale-cross-org metadata feeding resolvers is the drift class that resurfaces elsewhere.

Refs #4473 (PR #4483), #4252 (the denied-vs-unpublished half, backend gate objectstack#8013 merged as #8135).

Filed unassigned for triage.
